title.en: How to group plants and how to group animals

text.en:
Ravi sorted plants in his garden into big and small ones.
"Scientists group them in better ways," said his teacher.

We group plants by size and stem: herbs are small with soft stems, shrubs are bushy with woody stems and trees are tall with thick trunks. Climbers and creepers need support or spread on the ground.
Animals can be grouped by whether they have a backbone: vertebrates like fish, birds and mammals, and invertebrates like insects and worms. They can also be grouped by what they eat or where they live.
Grouping helps us study the huge variety of life.

problem.en: Group a rose bush and a mango tree.

text.en: A rose bush is bushy: a shrub.
A mango tree is tall with a trunk: a tree.
They differ in size and stem.

prompt.en: A friend says a snail has a backbone. How will you reply?

points.en: Animals can have or lack a backbone.
